correctness.summary: Double-counting the inclusion graph between s-component and (s-1)-component forests gives a general lower bound (n-s+1)/(m-n+s). In K_n, every s-forest has at least C(n,2)-C(n-s+1,2) valid one-edge extensions, yielding the matching complete-graph upper bound. The missing-edge hypothesis compares these denominators exactly. Equality cases are separated by the alternate component profile (n-s,2,1,...) and the top two ranks. Direct graph-atlas verification found no counterexample.

originality.scope: to the best of our knowledge
originality.summary: The September 2026 Bencs--Csikvari preprint states the consecutive-ratio assertion as Conjecture 5.8 and proves the s=2 case, but the inspected text does not give the missing-edge threshold, the m <= 3n-6 regime, or the planar consequence. Exact and synonymous searches found no equivalent statement. Residual risk comes from older forest-enumeration literature and an unpublished Eaton--Kook--Thoma monotonicity manuscript that may overlap with the complete-graph sequence ingredient.

value.summary: The result proves the recent stronger spanning-forest ratio conjecture for every connected graph with at most 3n-6 edges, hence for every connected planar graph, and gives a sharper levelwise criterion for arbitrary graphs in terms of their number of missing edges.

limitations: The edge threshold is sufficient and is not claimed necessary or sharp.
Low-component ratios of denser graphs remain unresolved except for the known universal s=2 case.
Teranishi (2005) and the unpublished Eaton--Kook--Thoma monotonicity manuscript were not fully inspected.
Finite verification supports but does not replace the proof.
Independent audit has not been performed.
